page: Amazon Web Services m6in.12xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance optimized for high-bandwidth networking and enterprise computing workloads. Driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor operating at 3.5 GHz. It provides 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not provided, requiring reliance on remote Elastic Block Store (EBS) volumes, but the platform features a substantial 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No physical GPUs are present.

Benchmark results highlight solid performance across standard general-purpose computing tasks. In CPU metrics, the instance achieves 46,377.4 in stress-ng multi-core testing, alongside a Geekbench multi-core score of 15,823.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 48,435.76, placing it squarely in the middle 50% tier. Instruction-set acceleration provides stronger outcomes in specialized areas: the instance scores in the top 25% for PassMark CPU encryption (43,448.8) and Geekbench image processing (15,040.0), supported by hardware-level AES, VAES, and AVX-512 extensions. Memory bandwidth reaches 158.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 69.22 GB/sec for writes.

Workload evaluation shows balanced execution across distributed serving and in-memory services. The instance records 45.59 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and delivers 41.66 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For CPU-based language model inference, it processes 91.95 prompt tokens per second and 25.02 generation tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. These metrics, combined with 75 Gbps of baseline networking, make m6in.12xlarge well positioned for high-traffic web applications, microservices backbones, clustered databases, and distributed ETL pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m6in.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz. Configured with 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores and 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory, it preserves a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It lacks local instance storage and dedicated GPUs, depending instead on network storage while offering 75 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Benchmarks display steady mid-tier results in stress-ng multi-core (46,377.4) and PassMark CPU tests (48,435.76), with upper-quartile scores in encryption tests (43,448.8) backed by cryptographic and AVX-512 instructions. The server yields 45.59 million Redis SET operations per second and 41.66 GB/sec in web throughput, making it suitable for distributed caching, high-concurrency web tiers, relational databases, and ETL processing.
